A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIT-GNN. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and changed experimental settings.

before.justification: v2 reports original node and graph classification/regression experiments, inference timings, memory measurements and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original FIT-GNN performance and resource measurements, including expanded architecture comparisons and full OGBN-Products evaluation.

M1.justification: The graph-level pooling procedure changes: v2 Algorithm 4 masks appended nodes before pooling, whereas v3 Algorithm 2 stacks all subgraph node representations without that mask. The underlying coarsening, Extra Nodes and Cluster Nodes procedures remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 13 datasets, four task families and four QM9 targets. Expanding OGBN-Products from a proxy to the full graph changes sampling and scale within retained product-classification coverage; this is assessed under E3.

E2.justification: v3 adds GCOND and BONSAI to node-classification comparisons and DOSCOND and KIDD to graph classification. It also adds full-graph and alternative-architecture baselines involving GAT, SAGE and GIN. Huang et al. (2021) is retained under the name SGGC.

E3.justification: Main node-classification results switch from coarsened-graph pretraining followed by subgraph training to subgraph-only training. Graph regression switches from Cluster Nodes to Extra Nodes, and architecture configurations expand. OGBN-Products performance evaluation grows from a 165,000-node proxy to the 2,449,029-node graph, while timing comparisons retain the proxy.

E4.justification: v3 removes the two-training-setup graph-classification comparison in v2 Table 7 and expands coarsening-ratio sweeps across architectures. The Extra/Cluster Nodes and six-coarsener studies remain in v3 Tables 15–17 with partly revised evidence; their relocation is not an addition.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports 20 runs or trials and summarizes the best 10 outcomes. v3 retains best-10 means and standard deviations but omits the total run count. This is reduced statistical disclosure, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Performance and memory tables are extensively revised and expanded, including architecture-specific results and full-Products accuracy/OOM entries. For example, Table 3's Chameleon result at r=0.1 changes from 0.460±0.002 to 0.496±0.005. The numerical inference timings in v2 Tables 10–11 remain unchanged in v3 Table 8; results under revised settings do not establish same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A.1 corrects the two-hop information-loss expression by also excluding V(Gi). Appendix C adds a time-gap derivation, the assumption max_i n_i=n/alpha, and feasibility analysis. The original two lemmas remain, although the new time-gap expansion contains a sign inconsistency relative to Equation 3.

C1.justification: v3 strengthens the claimed memory reduction from up to 70× to 100× and emphasizes processing extremely large graphs that baselines cannot handle. Its abstract replaces the assertion that graph-level coarsening applications were unexplored with extension language. The central inference-efficiency contribution remains.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies the complexity calculation as GCN-specific and explains node-level masking through possible test-node information in appended nodes. Section 6.1 strengthens graph-regression interpretation from comparable performance to superiority over baselines, although Table 6 contains exceptions. Existing neighborhood-information-loss qualifications largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 specifies per-class training/validation counts and supplies explicit coarsened-graph training pseudocode. It omits v2's MAE-normalization recipe and Leiden-based proxy-selection description. Core optimizer settings, epochs, hidden dimensions, hardware and the code destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially broadens positioning beyond sampling and coarsening to graph condensation, computational trees and graph-dataset distillation. Section 2 adds substantive discussion of GCOND, GC-SNTK, BONSAI, DOSCOND and KIDD, revising the account of prior graph-level work and the remaining research gap.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and methodological explanations are substantially rewritten. Related work moves before preliminaries, results become a separate main section, dataset setup is consolidated into a table, and appendices are reorganized with relocated proofs and algorithms.

P2.justification: v3 replaces Figure 1 with a pipeline overview, redraws Figure 3 as a multi-dataset logarithmic memory chart and adds feasibility Figure 4. Numerous tables are expanded, merged or relocated, alongside a document-wide switch from two-column to single-column layout.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens comparative evidence through relevant condensation baselines, additional architectures and full-Products evaluation. However, Table 5 compares different data splits, explicit run-count and normalization details disappear, and Appendix C introduces a sign error in its scaling derivation. Section 6.1 also overstates graph-regression superiority relative to Table 6. These substantive benefits and new reporting and reasoning weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
